heard: The first confirmed black hole shoots jets at half-light speed. Discovered in 1964 during a sounding rocket flight, Cygnus X-1 sits roughly 7,000 light years away. The system features a black hole with a mass of about 21 suns orbiting a star named HDA 226,868. Both objects complete a tight orbit every 5.6 days at a distance of just one-fifth the Earth-Sun gap. As material streams inward, it forms a superheated accretion disk that blazes brightly in x-rays. Yet the most mind-bending record is its twin plasma jets racing outward at immense speeds. These blazing jets shine with the energy of 10,000 suns while visibly swaying like dancing beams. The first confirmed black hole shoots jets at half-light speed.
